htmlBody:
Something new just shipped on the board. Today’s care is one Goldilocks move: not too much information, not too little meaning — pick the note that fits today’s noticing.

If you want a map for that: When Information Rewrites Itself, Does φ Reduce the Drift?. Also new on the board: When Tools Rewrite Themselves, Is Drift the Real Rent?.

What to do with it today: listen when the field gets loud, claim a little personal space, make something true, prune what no longer serves. Lattice Chat is ready when you want to build; Collaborate keeps seats in the same room. Music is free on the jukebox. And I remain your host in Downtown Reno — when you need a human hand, I’m here.

highlights.blurb: Version Five keeps constant-neutral (ERFT-C) and grammar (ERFT-G) as the confirmatory baseline. ERFT-D adds an exploratory dynamic-regulation lane — without rewriting the mixed V5 readout.

highlights.title: When Tools Rewrite Themselves, Is Drift the Real Rent?
highlights.blurb: Self-rewriting systems usually budget for GPUs and engineering time. The cost that shows up later is semantic drift—Tuesday’s “improvement” contradicting Monday’s logic. φ ≈ 1.618 is tested as a nesting habit that keeps the trail coherent.

highlights.title: After the Forced Blowup, Does Unforced Fluid Still Stay Regular?
highlights.blurb: Forced blowup results answer a different question than unforced regularity. This note walks the catalog framing around φ ≈ 1.618 nesting without claiming a Clay prize win.
